supporting_observations.claim: A network logon for sean.byrne to WS-ACOLE-01 was recorded shortly before the PowerShell process; the logon and PowerShell event share LogonId 0x1072f79b.

At 13:43 UTC, PowerShell ran the documented \FILE-ORC-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1 command as sean.byrne. This matches the documented IT workstation-patching practice, though the logs do not independently verify who initiated the session.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package from the local patches directory, then exited about 24 seconds after it started. This is consistent with the reported brief window and the documented patching activity.
PowerShell made a connection through the explicit proxy during execution, but the available Zeek record provides connection-level byte counts rather than the request destination or content.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:00 UTC, so there is no proxy record to identify or assess the PowerShell connection at 13:43. The sensor status supplied with the alert reports this collection outage.
The available records do not include the contents of Patch-Workstations.ps1 or telemetry showing what appeared on the user’s screen.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the person who initiated the sean.byrne session was sean.byrne, or map source IP 10.56.10.23 to WS-SBYRNE-01.
The destination and content of the PowerShell-associated proxy request are not established.
The evidence does not establish whether the user-visible PowerShell window was interactive or what the user saw.
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: SYSTEM on WS-ACOLE-01 explicitly attempted to use svc-safe credentials against DC-ORC-01 from taskhostw.exe. This is outside the alerted PowerShell activity; the inventory describes svc-safe as a backup agent account on FILE-ORC-01. (T294-00142)
